findings.passage: Two maps can have the same field count and total active area but different holes. As the activity threshold rises, active regions shrink and can split or disappear. The numbers of components and holes can change.
findings.sidecar_summary: Two maps can have the same field count and total active area but different holes. As the activity threshold rises, active regions shrink and can split or disappear. The numbers of components and holes can change.
findings.evidence: For q2>q1 the active set shrinks. The repair allows splitting/disappearance and changes in component/hole numbers, without the impossible joining claim. It leads correctly into the visible Euler characteristic definition, and agrees with the caption and nested-set alt text.
findings.caption: As the threshold rises on one constructed smooth map, components and holes change separately, giving Euler characteristics -1, 0, 4, and 3. The above-threshold regions shrink as the threshold rises, even though this signed count does not change in one direction. This guide example is not an observed place-field map or a Gaussian-process sample; it illustrates Mainali et al. (2025), Figure 3F–H and STAR Methods Equations 8–10.
findings.alt: Four thresholds of the same smooth two-dimensional map show one component with two holes and chi minus one; one component with one hole and chi zero; four components with no holes and chi four; and three components with no holes and chi three. Each active set is contained in the preceding one as q increases from 0.3 to 0.5, 0.8 and 1.0.

optional_title_recheck.title: Noise limits memory accuracy in continuous attractor models
optional_title_recheck.purpose: A stable population pattern can retain a continuous value while fluctuations move that value along its family of persistent states. These chapters establish the neural and probability background, derive the surviving motion, and connect it to limits on information and readout.
optional_title_recheck.evidence: The title now identifies continuous attractor models rather than all persistent-memory mechanisms. The purpose explains the persistent-state family and motion along it; Chapters 2 and 3 retain the detailed noise assumptions and lower-bound scope.
